title: Home feed service and its tests
name: Home feed assembly

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in these tests that could make any of them pass on some runs and fail on others? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: "orders posts newest first" builds the service with systemClock. The two publish calls usually happen within the same millisecond, so both posts get the same createdAt. The comparator then returns 0, the stable sort keeps insertion order (bob's post before carol's), and the test expecting [second, first] fails. It passes only when the clock happens to tick to the next millisecond between the two calls. The other tests use SteppingClock, which guarantees distinct timestamps, and this one should too.

choiceQuestions.prompt: In "respects the limit", why is the first returned post "post 4"?
choices: Because homeFeed reverses the per-author list before merging
Because Map iteration returns the most recently set entry first
Because the ids sort descending and the sort compares ids
Because SteppingClock gives each publish a timestamp 1 second later, and homeFeed sorts by createdAt descending
choiceQuestions.explanation: Each now() call adds 1000 ms, so post 4 has the largest createdAt, and the comparator b.createdAt - a.createdAt puts it first. No list is reversed, Map iteration is in insertion order, and the sort never looks at ids.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Two posts in the candidate list have identical createdAt values. How does homeFeed order them?
choices: In the order they were pushed into candidates, because Array.prototype.sort is stable
choiceQuestions.explanation: The comparator returns 0 for equal timestamps, and Array.prototype.sort has been stable since ES2019, so the posts keep their order in candidates: the user's own posts first, then followees in followeesOf order, each in publish order. There is no secondary key on id or authorId, and the order is deterministic, not random.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does the test file create a new FeedService inside each test instead of sharing one across the describe block?
choices: Posts and the id counter live in the instance, so a shared instance would leak posts between tests and make results depend on test order
FeedService cannot be constructed inside beforeEach
node:test runs tests in separate processes, so a shared instance would not be visible
homeFeed caches results per user on first call
choiceQuestions.explanation: postsByAuthor and seq are instance fields. With one shared service, posts from one test would show up in another test's feed and change counts and limits depending on run order. Constructing it in beforeEach would also work; tests in a file share one process; and homeFeed has no cache.
